assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of intracellular signaling, in which the endoplasmic reticulum communicates its folding state to the nucleus through IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and downstream stress pathways. It is original, mechanistically clear and conceptually general, and it underlies work on secretory physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The impact on cell biology and disease understanding is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Walter's laboratory identified IRE1 as the sensor and the unconventional HAC1 mRNA splicing mechanism, and Mori's work identified the UPR transcriptional program and the signaling link to the nucleus. Both are on the supplied credit list and together form a clean two-person configuration. Credit that may be owed to others, such as Kozutsumi or Sidrauski, is not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: The pathway has been confirmed independently over about three decades in yeast, metazoans and mammals, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is well timed. Therapeutic translation (for example ISRIB, IRE1 and PERK modulation) is still developing, but the basic discovery does not depend on it.
uncertainties: I am recalling the detailed priority contributions from memory and have not verified them against the sources.
Whether the committee wants a basic-mechanism prize whose clinical translation is incomplete.
Other contributors to the original discovery are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and the incretin-based therapies derived from it have changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. They combine basic physiology (the incretin effect and proglucagon processing) with therapies that have shown large effects on weight, glycemia and cardiovascular outcomes. Importance, scale of patient benefit and current prominence are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are spread across several people. Holst characterized the physiology of the active GLP-1 peptides, Drucker established gut-derived GLP-1 biology and its therapeutic uses, Mojsov contributed to identifying the active peptide, and Knudsen led the development of long-acting analogues. Habener, who is not on the supplied list, also seems relevant to this history. The three-name limit makes the allocation hard. I propose Holst, Drucker and Knudsen as the physiology-to-therapy configuration, and recognize that Mojsov's claim is a real unresolved issue.
assessment.maturity: Phase 3 trials and real-world use confirm the therapies independently, and the physiological basis is stable. Timing is strong, although long-term safety and the full range of indications are still being defined.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among the four credited people and an uncredited contributor is disputed and I have not verified the details.
Whether a prize should recognize the physiology, the drug development, or both, given the industry component.
Long-term outcomes of these therapies are not yet fully known.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR defined the nutrient- and growth-factor-sensing kinase hub that controls cell growth, metabolism and autophagy. It began with genetic work in yeast and became a central framework for metabolism, aging, cancer and immunosuppression. The concept is original, general and broadly influential.
assessment.attribution: Hall's group identified TOR genetically and showed it as the target of rapamycin, which is the decisive discovery. Schreiber's chemical-biology work on rapamycin, FKBP12 and the drug-protein complex was a foundational part of the route to TOR. Sabatini made important mammalian mTORC1 and nutrient-sensing contributions, but I leave him out of the proposal because the mTOR biology is large and the three-person limit forces a choice, and because I am uncertain about the circumstances of his later career. Brown, Sabers and others would also have strong claims, but are not on this list.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is strongly confirmed across species and models, with many clinical offshoots (rapalogs in transplantation and oncology). Recognition is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Several key people, including mammalian TOR discoverers not on the supplied list, create a real allocation problem.
Whether the committee views Schreiber's role as part of the discovery or as chemical biology adjacent to it.
My recall of the detailed priority history is from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave a general method to control the activity of genetically defined cells with light, and it changed circuit neuroscience, behavior research and some translational work (vision restoration). The discovery is original, built on microbial rhodopsin biophysics and then turned into a tool, and its impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: The decisive steps were the characterization of channelrhodopsin (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg), the demonstration of neuronal control (Boyden and Deisseroth, and Bamberg's group), and the earlier genetic photostimulation concept (Miesenböck). Six people are credited, so any three-name configuration leaves out someone with a real claim. I propose Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel as the most defensible, but this is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: The method is thoroughly reproduced across laboratories and species and is a routine tool. Clinical use is still limited (early retinal work), but as a methods and discovery prize the maturity is high. It is a technology-heavy candidate within a prize that is for discovery.
uncertainties: Contested allocation among six credited people, including Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck.
Whether tools and methods are weighed enough against a physiological discovery.
Clinical translation is early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living therapies. The concept, the receptor design with costimulation, and the clinical proof are important and have had large impact on cancer treatment, and are now extending to autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain's work on costimulated CARs, June's clinical translation in CLL and ALL, and Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T-cell trials together form a plausible three-person configuration. Eshhar, Kuwana and others with early design claims are not on the supplied list, and that is a real gap in the credit story.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and consistent response rates across independent centers confirm the efficacy. Toxicity, relapse and solid-tumor limits remain, but the interpretation of the core advance is stable, and recognition seems timely.
uncertainties: Priority issues: early CAR design credit (not on the supplied list) is unresolved.
Whether Rosenberg's role is the key adoptive therapy contribution or a separate one.
Limits in solid tumors and durability.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and the BCR-ABL concept established rational targeted therapy, turning chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a chronic manageable one. It is a model for the translation of a molecular lesion into a specific drug, with very large patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the discovery of the compound at Ciba-Geigy, Druker led the clinical proof and the drive to trials, and Sawyers contributed the resistance mechanisms and the next-generation inhibitors. This is a clean three-person translational configuration. Rowley's and Witte's, and others', earlier contributions to the BCR-ABL discovery are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: It has been confirmed over more than two decades of clinical use, and the mechanism and resistance biology are well understood. Recognition is mature, and some may argue it is overdue, but the Lasker already honored it.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers the earlier BCR-ABL discoveries as the more fundamental part, which would complicate the configuration.
Industry versus academic credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING is the central pathway for sensing cytosolic DNA in innate immunity. It connects the second messenger cGAMP, the sensor and the adaptor to interferon and inflammatory responses, with implications for infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and aging. It is original and has had a rapid broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen's group identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide cGAMP second messenger, which is the central molecular discovery. Barber identified STING. Ishikawa, Wu and Sun are also credited, but their contributions look secondary to the two proposed, as far as I recall. The configuration with Chen and Barber is reasonably clear.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is extensively confirmed and the structural and cell biology are well understood. Therapeutic translation (agonists, inhibitors) has not yet delivered an approved drug, so recognition may be somewhat early, though the fundamental discovery is mature enough.
uncertainties: Priority among STING discoverers (several groups reported STING in 2008 to 2009), which is not fully resolved.
Therapeutic validation is still pending.
My recollection of the contributions is from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, and gave a proof of principle for splicing-directed RNA therapeutics. The advance links basic splicing mechanism with a transformative treatment for a devastating pediatric disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer's work defined the splicing regulatory elements and the antisense strategy for SMN2 exon 7 inclusion, and Bennett led the development of the antisense chemistry and the drug at Ionis. The two-person configuration is clear. Other contributors, such as Singh, Hua and the SMN gene discovery (Melki and Lefebvre), are outside this credit and may matter.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy has been confirmed in trials and long-term use, and the approach has been extended. Recognition is timely, although the broader antisense field has had mixed results and the prize question may be whether the RNA-therapeutics principle is sufficiently general.
uncertainties: Whether an SMA-specific therapy is broad enough, or if it would be better combined with other RNA therapeutics.
Contributions of the SMN1 gene discovery are not credited here.
Treatment benefit varies with age at treatment.
